calls.title: EA + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The meeting centered around EA's evaluation of GrowthBook as a replacement for AWS regarding feature management and configuration. The player experience team is testing GrowthBook for its ability to handle real-time feature toggling without the need for server restarts, which has been a limitation with AWS. The proof of concept (POC) involves around 80 users and aims to explore GrowthBook's enterprise features like SSO and environment inheritance. Pricing discussions revealed an annual fee structure and considerations for self-hosting versus SaaS options, highlighting security as a primary concern for EA. Next steps involve an internal review of pricing and features, with a follow-up call scheduled to address further inquiries.
calls.keywords: feature management, self-hosted, enterprise pricing, SSO, environment inheritance, AWS alternatives

calls.title: EA + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The team discussed significant budget constraints, highlighting an inability to cover a $200k enterprise license due to current financial limitations and the necessity for SSO. Abhinav Kulshrestha emphasized that although the enterprise plan offers many features, they require a custom solution for security. The player experience team lacks allocated funds for feature flagging until new budget streams arise after December. Challenges with existing AWS flagging slowing release velocity were noted, prompting interest in improving DORA metrics. A demo of GrowthBook illustrated its environment inheritance and feature rollout capabilities, enabling complex configurations and integration with existing workflows. Controlled rollouts were discussed, including automatic rollback based on data, and the need for caching was highlighted to improve performance and stability. Team collaboration features were also examined, along with potential scalability.
calls.keywords: feature flags, budget constraints, single sign-on, environment inheritance, rollout ramp-up, caching strategies

calls.title: EA + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The meeting covered the complexities surrounding the pilot migration to a warehouse-native model on Snowflake, highlighting issues with multiple telemetry schemas and the need for collaboration with Snowflake admins. There was a significant focus on the declining quality of support following an acquisition, contrasting with previous responsive support from Statsig. Additionally, challenges in standardizing experimentation metrics and mapping user intent to business outcomes led to operational friction. The discussion also addressed competitive dynamics in the market, noting Amplitude's push for leadership despite customer dissatisfaction, while Growth Book positions itself as a responsive, developer-friendly alternative. Finally, a product roadmap focused on warehouse-native features and AI-driven experimentation was outlined, along with next steps for deeper collaboration.
calls.keywords: warehouse migration, experimentation platform, data telemetry, feature gates, support quality, open source experimentation
